links.targetTitle: PinkRoccade (Healthcare / Local Gov) — own vertical products

title: PinkRoccade has ideal healthcare and municipal verticals but sells products rather than custom builds
content:
The flag on PinkRoccade puts the verdict plainly: the verticals are ideal but the business model is product, not custom. Healthcare and municipalities are exactly the buyers the pilot wants to reach, and the firm's platforms are its own vertical products.

A product company and a custom-build partner monetise different things — a roadmap versus delivery hours — and only the second has a commercial reason to place someone else's component in front of a client. That is why sector fit alone cannot rescue the row, and it is the same conclusion the Portuguese healthtech row for Glintt reaches independently.

The second half of the flag is a data-quality warning: all financials are stale by fifteen years, including the recorded revenue of 197 million. Any sizing judgement built on that figure is unsupported. It joins Valcon's pre-merger revenue and Sopra Steria Netherlands' post-merger figures as a recurring problem in the Dutch rows — the revenue column is present far more often than it is current.
